title: Music Player
mainDescription: A web-based music player application that allows users to listen to their favorite songs, create playlists, and customize their listening experience.
secondaryDescription:
The app has:

  • its backend built with .NET to get the songs locally and serve an API with features like streaming songs, getting albums / artists, etc.
  • its frontend powered by Angular, which features an user-friendly interface

title: code-cluster
mainDescription:
An archive of problems which tackle subjects such as: dynamic programming, data structures or programming done in languages like: c++, python, java, typescript, etc.

From getting error values of a dataset by training a linear regression model, to training a logistic regression model for predicting digits from images, the repository covers a wide range of topics. Other examples would be a simulation for a movie recommendation platform in java and an implementation of pushdown automata algorithm in c++.

title: iungOreal
mainDescription:
A fullstack social media project where its name is a wordplay for 'going outside' (“iungo” means “to connect” in Latin) which aims to guide users into participating at outdoor events taking place in their city (marked on the integrated map) and share their experiences with others.

Users can: post and comment on made posts, discuss in private / group / regional chats, update their profile to their liking and many other interactions just like in a typical social media website.
secondaryDescription: The project is based on a microservice architecture, having as frameworks Spring Boot server-side and Angular client-side. Most notable tools used include: spring-boot-starter for productivity in: security, web, db management & development overall; JUnit, Mockito and H2 for unit and integration tests, awssdk to connect to a cloud service, stompjs for websocket connection and leaflet for implementation of the map.

title: InfOpescuit V2
mainDescription:
A desktop app which solves the mundane and error-prone way of taking reports of check-ins and check-outs for fishing lakes. InfOpescuit acts as a payment gateway, where the user scans barcodes of customer's cards to automate the process of writing data in excels and calculating revenue at closing.

It improves the time taken to fill in excel data by hand by at least 12 times and it sees human errors occurring less than about 20 times, having less unnecesary room exposed and given the fact that navigation through the app is more pleasant to the eye.
secondaryDescription: It is written in Python but compiled in C++ for faster speeds at runtime. The UI is done with Tkinter, OpenPyxl is used for excel manipulation, whereas Fernet, hmac, symmetric and asymmetric keys are applied for security purposes. Besides some other features it also includes conversion of tables to csv and xml (with custom mappings).

title: StreetArt Platform
mainDescription:
A web platform designed for both mobile and desktop users, where artists can reserve performance venues and users can view events and their locations.

Instead of lots of paperwork, everything is done through the platform, as a central place for everybody. It speeds up the whole process of booking venues, having a committee approve or decline artists, and its the best way of informing users in regard to artists in the area.
secondaryDescription:
Its backend is powered by Spring Boot, and frontend is built with Angular. Important technologies and tools used include:

  • leaflet for the map functionality
  • aws s3 as an object storage solution to add, remove and retrieve images used throughout the app
  • firebase as an email verification service
  • spring-security for authentication and authorization
  • database management - is done through MySql for data storage and is implemented through spring data's jpa, amazon's rds being used as the cloud-hosted db solution
  • deployment - has been done on a (docker-integrated) ubuntu virtual machine (provided by DigitalOcean). Microservices run on containers, while the client app has its static files served through an nginx reverse-proxy, which also handles request redirection, implements rate-limiting and switches to access by https.
  • testing environment - currently consists of only unit tests: JUnit5+Mockito for backend (coverage stats provided through 'JaCoCo' plugin) and jasmine+Karma for frontend (coverage stats provided by Karma's istanbul).

title: InfOpescuit V3
mainDescription:
The updated version of its predecessor, which feels more robust and less like a prototype. Designed fully local for both Computers and Android tablets, it does what version 2 does and much more.

New functionalities include:

  • a sheet viewer for checking and changing data for excel sheets without leaving the application
  • cash register integration when doing check-ins / check-outs
  • new sheet integrations for promotions and reservations
  • custom report data per lake
  • language switching
  • and many more
secondaryDescription: It is developed in Flutter, leveraging different libraries like: flutter_excel for doing operations on .xlsx files, trina_grid for rendering tables inside the app, barcode_widget to display barcodes as images, pasteboard to copy barcode images or taking snapshots of reports, etc.

title: AsigurAZ
mainDescription:
A cross-platform car insurance application built for Web, Android, and iOS. It features a straightforward, intuitive UI that simplifies the insurance process.

Users can easily generate and compare custom offers and once a specific coverage option is chosen, the payment process unfolds. Active, paid policies become immediately accessible for viewing directly within the app, and a PDF copy is automatically dispatched to the user's email after a successful payment.

The application can be found at: https://autoaaz.ro, or it can be downloaded from play store or app store.
secondaryDescription:
Technical Stack & Key Features:

  • Frontend: Built with Flutter for cross-platform deployment across Web, Android, and iOS.
  • Backend & Infrastructure: Serverless Node.js environment hosted on Google Cloud Platform via Firebase.
  • Security & Authentication: Secured using Firebase Authentication, App Check, and Secrets Manager.
  • Payment Processing: Integrated with Netopia, handling transactions asynchronously via webhooks.
  • Other features: Rate Limiting managed through an Upstash Redis database, Emails are dispatched using Mailtrap, etc.
